Query county-level IPEDS data from S3

dot-ipeds_county_query.Rd

Queries the processed county-level parquet files from S3 via DuckDB. Returns the 6-column tidy format: one row per county / year / variable.

Usage

.ipeds_county_query(
  years = NULL,
  geoids = NULL,
  variables = NULL,
  surveys = NULL,
  s3_bucket = "cori.data.ipeds",
  s3_path_prefix = ""
)

Arguments

years

Integer vector. Years to return. Default: all available.

geoids

Character vector. 5-digit county FIPS codes to return. Default: all counties.

variables

Character vector. Variable names to return (e.g. "completions_total", "grad_rate_150pct"). Default: all. Call get_ipeds_codebook() for the full list.

surveys

Character vector. One or more of "institutional_characteristics", "completions", "completers", "grad_rates". Default: all.

s3_bucket

Character. S3 bucket name. Default: "cori.data.ipeds".

s3_path_prefix

Character. Optional path prefix (e.g. "test/"). Default: "".

Value

A data frame with columns: geoid (character, 5-digit FIPS), year (integer), variable (character), value (numeric), agg_var (numeric), survey (character).

Note that completions variables count awards while completers variables count students, so the two are not interchangeable and the count_students_* variables must not be summed across award levels.

Details

County data combines all three IPEDS surveys (IC, completions, graduation rates) into a single table. Use the surveys argument to filter to a specific survey, or variables to select specific metrics.

See also

get_ipeds(), get_ipeds_codebook()

Note this differs from get_ipeds(), which takes survey first and requires it. Here every filter is optional and years comes first, so pass the survey by name: get_ipeds(surveys = "completions"), not get_ipeds("completions"). Passing it positionally used to return zero rows silently; it now errors.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# All county data for Grafton County NH
get_ipeds(geoids = "33009")

# Graduation rates for all counties, 2015-2023
get_ipeds(
  variables = "grad_rate_150pct",
  years     = 2015:2023
)
} # }
